topic: catalog capacity reservations
canonical_claim: Catalog admission must reserve each entry's worst-case Removing and fold-seal representation so capacity can never refuse the transition needed to remove an admitted entry. Catalog admission must reject creation unless the encoded catalog plus worst-case fold cursor and removal reservations fit within both the catalog cap and the 256 MiB fold-seal cap. Catalog admission must enforce the additive reservation predicate fold_fixed + Σ reserve_cursor(entry) + Σ reserve_removing_cleanup(entry) + Σ reserve_hold(entry) <= fold_seal_cap in addition to encoded_catalog(post).size <= catalog_cap.

topic: Arithmetic exact key intake is the

topic: A proposed manifest cache is keyed
canonical_claim: A proposed manifest cache is keyed by `ManifestId`, scoped to one fold round, bounded in bytes, and dropped at round end; avoiding one redundant edge avoids both its HEAD and GET trips. The useful manifest-body cache scope is one GC round: an op-scoped or transaction-scoped cache saves nothing, while a round-scoped cache can avoid cross-transaction re-reads; the HEAD-before-GET pair remains vetoed from change. In the measured intake, 7,565 edge reads were re-reads across 4,573 distinct manifests, or 39.6%; all observed re-reads were cross-transaction and none were intra-transaction. In that fold window, 2,991 manifests carried both an add and a remove edge, and `CasManifestGet == CasRefEmittedEdges`, demonstrating that no manifest-body cache existed. 39.6% of GC intake manifest fetches are re-reads (7,565 edges over 4,573 distinct manifests): intra-transaction redundancy is exactly zero, and all of it is cross-transaction (2,991 manifests carry both an add and a remove edge in the window, so the same body is read once when the ref is published and again when it is dropped), making a round-scoped body cache — not an op- or transaction-scoped one — the effective lever.

topic: GC streams the three cursor merge
canonical_claim: GC streams the three-cursor merge but accumulates the round's `std::vector<BlobDelta>` in memory, so a large mass-drop delta can cause an OOM and repeated lack of progress for that shard.

topic: Task A7 serializes the manual SYSTEM
canonical_claim: Task A7 serializes the manual `SYSTEM ... GC` round against the background GC loop using a dedicated gc_round_mutex rather than the scheduler's existing `mutex`, because loop() deliberately releases `mutex` before running a round so that stop() and heartbeatLoop() are not blocked; holding `mutex` across a long fold would freeze the GC heartbeat and stall shutdown.

topic: A destructive GC gate based only
canonical_claim: A destructive GC gate based only on `proven == total` accepts an empty universe vacuously because `0 == 0`; the fix adds an explicit nonempty-authority predicate so the gate cannot be satisfied by having nothing to prove.; The empty `CaGcDestructiveGateCore` universe configuration was green, with `CatalogUniverse = FrontierProven = {}` and physical actions suppressed despite the two sets being equal.

topic: cas gc rebuild s security verdict
canonical_claim: `cas-gc-rebuild`'s security verdict: it cannot delete live data directly (deletions still flow through the normal round's ack-floor plus two-phase plus exact-token path), and a crafted owner state that makes rebuild under-count requires full owner-plane write access, which already implies total pool compromise (SEC-3) — the trimmed-history guard closes the naive truncation path. Residual risks: FORCE only skips the healthy-pool check (operational risk, not a safety bypass); rebuild does a full-universe discover-and-fold (O(all shards + all journals)), an expensive pool-wide sweep an attacker with SYSTEM access could trigger repeatedly (shares the SEC-4 decode/fold exhaustion surface); and a concurrent GC leader's round CAS and rebuild's `gc/state` install can contend, so rebuild must be verified to respect GC leadership or a split-baseline is possible.

topic: D7 the SQL SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED
canonical_claim: D7: the SQL `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD` verb and the offline `clickhouse-disks ca-gc-rebuild` command are NOT duplication — both call the same `Gc::rebuildBaseline` core through two deliberately inverse-gated surfaces (live/writable vs offline/read-only), and this dual surface should be kept as-is.

topic: There are two independent sharding axes
canonical_claim: There are two independent sharding axes in GC that are deliberately different and easy to confuse: `blobShard` (blob-hash high64 % gc_shards, for in-degree work) versus `Store::shardOf` (CityHash64(ref_name) % root_shards, for the owner journal). There are also two independent lease/watermark concepts: the GC lease inside `gc/state`, versus the mount lease / build watermark at `gc/server-roots/<srid>/mount`; `computeHeartbeatFloor` fences only the latter, never the GC lease.

topic: The RemovalReady state costs less wire
canonical_claim: The RemovalReady state costs less wire-format surface than a life-keyed-cursor alternative: cursor identity appears in eight files spanning the wire grammar, every builder/parser, REBUILD, fsck, and the sweep's coverage lookup, versus one enum value, one codec branch, one transition, and the five predicate sites for RemovalReady. Life-keyed cursors also create a new corner case (a reborn name's fresh-life cursor coexists with a dead-life cursor nothing prunes), so they only relocate the retirement-tracking problem rather than avoiding it.

topic: The Stage B strategic review s
canonical_claim: The Stage B strategic review's invariant rulings: weaken byte-exact fold-seal capacity reservation to a generous over-covering bound (count times a conservative constant, hard namespace cap ~10^4) instead of exact worst-case arithmetic; cut the `Creating`-forbids-publication write-path check as a separate production-path obligation since `resolveNamespaceLife` already loops until `Live` and is the sole life source; cut incarnation-scoped fold cursor re-keying once prune-before-entry-delete is the pinned invariant; weaken the `_ckpt` conflict-is-corruption join to a semantic-max merge (corruption only on genuinely incomparable fields).
